content: Fosfomycin is an antibiotic used to treat bladder infections, such as acute cystitis or lower urinary tract infections, primarily in women. It works by inhibiting bacterial growth, specifically targeting bacterial cell wall synthesis through the inactivation of the enzyme pyruvyl transferase. This results in bactericidal effects. It is not effective against viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Administration Instructions: Fosfomycin is typically taken as a single oral dose of 3 grams. Before administration, dissolve the contents of one sachet (3 grams) in 4 ounces (120 milliliters) of cold water. Do not use warm or hot water. Stir until fully dissolved and consume immediately. Symptoms of the infection should improve within 2 to 3 days. If symptoms persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. Pharmacokinetics: Absorption: Rapidly absorbed with a bioavailability of 37% when fasting and 30% when taken with food. Time to Peak: Approximately 2 hours in serum. Volume of Distribution (Vd): 90-180 liters, with high concentrations achieved in urine and penetration into other tissues, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in cases of inflamed meninges. Half-life: 3-8 hours in individuals with normal renal function; prolonged to 50 hours in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl <10 mL/min). Excretion: Primarily excreted in urine (38% as unchanged drug), maintaining high urinary levels (>100 mcg/mL) for over 48 hours. Fecal excretion accounts for approximately 18%. Contraindications and Precautions: Fosfomycin is contraindicated for the treatment of perinephric abscesses or pyelonephritis. It is not recommended for use in patients with persistent or recurrent bacteriuria; alternative agents should be considered. Safety and efficacy in certain populations, such as pregnant or lactating women, have not been fully established. While it is excreted in breast milk, the risk to nursing infants is considered low. Use with caution in patients with a history of hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. Discontinue immediately if signs of hypersensitivity occur and provide supportive care. Prolonged use may lead to bacterial or fungal superinfections, which can manifest up to two months after antibiotic treatment. Monitor liver function during treatment, as hepatic injury, including hepatitis and steatosis, has been reported. These effects are reversible upon discontinuation of the drug. Drug Interactions: Fosfomycin may reduce the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid, cholera, or BCG vaccines) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. It may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of oral contraceptives, conjugated estrogens, and other hormone-based therapies. While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with metoclopramide may reduce the absorption of fosfomycin, leading to decreased therapeutic efficacy. Monitor for reduced effectiveness if these agents are used together. Fosfomycin may also interfere with the metabolism of certain drugs, such as sodium picosulfate, by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Side Effects: Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, headache, dizziness, fatigue, rash, and pruritus. Rare but serious side effects include severe intestinal conditions caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile)-associated diarrhea, which may occur during or after treatment. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylactic shock, have been reported. Hepatic injury, such as hepatitis or steatosis, may occur and requires monitoring of liver function. Special Populations: Pregnancy: Classified as Category B. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Use only when clearly needed. Lactation: Excreted in breast milk in small amounts; not recommended unless necessary. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., contact poison control at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Additional Notes: This medication is prescribed for your current condition only. Do not share it with others. Laboratory tests, such as urine cultures, may be performed during treatment to monitor effectiveness. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. This summary provides essential information but does not replace professional medical advice. Always follow your healthcare provider's instructions.
